reasons.A: Even, plain, modern-essay sentences with a hedging first-person ('I suspect'); no rhetorical questions, semicolon play or ironic snap, so it lacks the passage's arch, exclamatory energy.
reasons.B: Closest movement: long semicolon-joined sentences broken by short ironic snaps ('It exists chiefly in essays.'), rhetorical questions and a wry, mock-lofty stance close to the passage's own.
reasons.C: Catches the irony and some rhetorical questioning, but leans on runs of very short declaratives and anaphoric repetition ('He is... He is...') that the passage never uses, and has almost no semicolons or period flourish.
